claims.source_quote_ar: وَما مِنْ إِلهٍ إِلَّا إِلهٌ واحِدٌ
claims.claim_ar: استخدام تركيب «ما ... إلا» للحصر والتأكيد على استغراق التوحيد: لا إله قط إلا إله واحد.
claims.claim_en: The phrase 'ما من إله إلا إله واحد' employs the 'ما ... إلا' construction to restrict and emphatically assert exclusivity (there is no deity except the One God), reinforcing monotheism.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Strengthens the doctrinal assertion of tawhid by excluding any possible plurality of deity; creates categorical, unequivocal denial of partners to God.

claims.claim_ar: تكرير الشهادة عليهم بالكفر في افتتاح الآية وذكرهم بصيغة التكرار لشدّة الإدانة.
claims.claim_en: Repetition of the accusation of their disbelief: the verse repeats and foregrounds the statement that 'those who said (so) have indeed disbelieved', intensifying the condemnation.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Heightens moral/religious censure and rhetorical force by restating and emphasising their culpability.

claims.source_quote_ar: لَيَمَسَّنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
claims.claim_ar: استخدام صيغة التأكيد «لَيَمَسَّنَّ» بصيغة مستقبلية مؤكَّدة (اللام المشدّدة والنون) للتوكيد على حتمية الوعيد وشدّته.
claims.claim_en: The emphatic predictive construction 'لَيَمَسَّنَّ' (with emphatic lam and doubled nun) is used to strongly assert/forecast that a painful punishment will surely befall those among them who disbelieve.
claims.needs_review_reason: Labelled as 'ijab_inshaa' to capture emphatic predictive force; mapping of this Arabic rhetorical phenomenon to the exact subtype name should be reviewed by a specialist (could alternatively be labelled as a specific emphatic future construction).
claims.rhetorical_effect: Conveys inevitability and severity of divine punishment, prompting fear and seriousness in the addressee.
